source.title: Understanding the Effect of the Long Tail on Neural Network Compression
source.authors: Harvey Dam; Vinu Joseph; Aditya Bhaskara; Ganesh Gopalakrishnan; Saurav Muralidharan; Michael Garland

record.tranche_reason: The study estimates training-example influence and tests whether compression-induced prediction mismatches are associated with influence. This conceptually tests V8's link between influential/memorized examples and generalization-related outcomes, using compression mismatches rather than removing examples and measuring test accuracy.
record.gate_note: The paper measures influence and compares influence on compression-impacted exemplars (CIEs) with influence on non-CIEs. Other reported influence histograms and CIE counts are not rows: the former describe influence distributions without a claim-version outcome, and CIE counts alone do not measure the influence relationship.
record.test_reason: The study uses the memorization–generalization account and influence estimation to interpret compression mismatches. It does not test V8's intervention: removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples and comparing retrained test accuracy. Its compression–influence association measures a different outcome, and no other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately captures the authors' interpretation: compression mismatches tend to occur on test examples whose classification correctness depends more on training-example inclusion. The evidence is preliminary: the mismatch analysis uses ResNet-56 on CIFAR-10, and only two compression loss functions yielded statistically significant comparisons. It does not establish the test-accuracy effect of removing highly memorized examples.
record.recipe_differences: Estimates influence using repeated training on masked subsets, then relates influence to prediction mismatches after model compression; it does not remove high-influence examples and measure test accuracy.
record.method_sensitivity: Compression loss function and CIE type; statistical significance differed by loss function.

fits_no_version.finding: For compressed ResNet-56 on CIFAR-10, every tested compression loss produced some positive t-statistic comparing mean influence on compression-mismatched versus other test examples; two loss functions produced a result with p ≤ 0.05 (Section 3, Figure 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test examples whose predictions change after compression tend to have higher estimated mean influence from training examples than test examples whose predictions remain unchanged.

record.peer_reviewed: ICLR 2023 Workshop on Sparsity in Neural Networks
record.problems: CIFAR-10 only; experiments use ResNet-56 for compression mismatch analysis. The reported comparison is a t-test whose results are presented as a figure, with only two loss functions stated to meet p-value ≤ 0.05. No direct example-removal effect on test accuracy is measured.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: the reported result is a figure-only t-test relationship between influence and compression mismatch, and the paper does not report per-condition numeric values or a separately stated result that can be entered as a row under the claim's defined outcomes.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under natural versus random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under controlled epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples, retraining, and comparing test accuracy; dataset differences in that effect.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's V8 status from tested_not_extracted to not_tested. Random subset masking estimates influence; it is not targeted removal of highly memorized examples with a random-removal control. The empty rows and labels are appropriate for the supplied claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweep and test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train-test gap.

The study compares influence on compression mismatches, rather than removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change. It does not report the V8 removal intervention.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
